description: The number 802 does not appear as an explicit figure in the biblical text and has no known symbolic role in biblical numerology or Jewish tradition. versions.meaning: Number of priests who served in the temple in Jerusalem
versions.description: The number 802 appears in Nehemiah 11:12, where it indicates the number of priests who carried out work in the temple after returning from the Babylonian exile. The context is Nehemiah's list of those who settled in Jerusalem following its reconstruction, and the figure highlights the scope of the restored temple worship. Although 802 is not assigned broad symbolic meaning in Jewish tradition, its occurrence testifies to the extensive priesthood required to maintain daily sacrifices and temple operations during the Second Temple period.

footnotes.text: In Nehemiah 11:12, Adaiah son of Jeroham is mentioned in connection with these priests. The verse is part of a larger listing of family heads and their lineages who served in the temple after the exile.

Through gematria, 802 can be written using the Hebrew letters tav (400) + tav (400) + bet (2), but there is no known tradition that assigns a specific symbolic interpretation to this letter combination.
